Timing/onset and associated acute features: very sudden focal onset ± severe occipital headache, vomiting, or rapid deterioration (favours cerebellar stroke/hemorrhage) vs subacute progression over days/weeks with prior neurologic episodes or optic neuritis (favours MS) vs rapid onset after alcohol ingestion or exposure history (favours intoxication).
Urine/blood toxicology and blood ethanol level: positive/therapeutic levels consistent with impairment (supports intoxication) and absence argues against intoxication as cause.

Brain MRI pattern: single focal cerebellar diffusion lesion in a vascular territory (supports infarct) or hemorrhagic signal on CT/MRI (supports bleed) vs multiple periventricular/juxtacortical/cerebellar demyelinating plaques with contrast enhancement/dissemination in time (supports MS).
